claims.claim: Chipotle operates a restaurant‑based business that owns and operates the majority of its locations in the United States, Canada and Europe.
claims.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we owned 3,938 Chipotle restaurants throughout the United States (“U.S.”) and 104 international Chipotle restaurants. Additionally, we had 14 international partner‑operated restaurants… We manage our U.S. operations based on 11 regions and aggregate our operations to one reportable segment. Our revenue is derived from sales by our restaurants.

claims.claim: Management’s “Recipe for Growth” strategy is anchored on modernizing the business model with AI‑enabled technology and a relaunched Rewards program.
claims.quote: Modernize our business model with industry‑leading technology, including leveraging AI and relaunching our Rewards Program, to elevate the experience for our guests and teams.

claims.claim: Digital ordering is a core growth driver, accounting for more than one‑third of food‑and‑beverage revenue in 2025.
claims.quote: Digital sales represented 36.7% of food and beverage revenue in 2025, compared to 35.1% in 2024.

claims.claim: Chipotle is expanding its drive‑through‑style “Chipotlane” format to improve guest convenience and sales at new restaurants.
claims.quote: Chipotlanes continue to perform well and are helping enhance guest access and convenience, as well as increase new restaurant sales, margins and returns.

claims.claim: Management projects 350–370 new restaurant openings in 2026, roughly 80 % of which will feature a Chipotlane, and 10–15 additional partner‑operated sites internationally.
claims.quote: •350 to 370 new restaurant openings, which includes 10 to 15 international partner‑operated restaurants. Around 80% of new company‑owned restaurants will have a Chipotlane

claims.claim: For 2026 management expects full‑year comparable restaurant sales growth in the low single‑digit range.
claims.quote: •Full year comparable restaurant sales growth in the low single digit range

claims.claim: Management anticipates comparable restaurant sales to be roughly flat for the full year 2026.
claims.quote: For 2026, management is anticipating comparable restaurant sales to be about flat.

claims.claim: In Q3 2026 Chipotle opened 84 company‑owned restaurants, 53 of which included a Chipotlane, and added five international partner‑operated restaurants.
claims.quote: Opened 84 company‑owned restaurants, with 53 locations including a Chipotlane. We also opened five international partner‑operated restaurants.

claims.claim: Digital sales rose to 38.8% of total food‑and‑beverage revenue in Q3 2026, up from 36.7% a year earlier.
claims.quote: Digital sales represented 38.8% of total food and beverage revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase from 36.7% for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

claims.claim: Food, beverage and packaging costs fell to 29.5% of revenue in Q3 2026, down from 30.0% in the prior year.
claims.quote: Food, beverage and packaging costs in the third quarter of 2026 were 29.5% of total revenue, a decrease from 30.0% in the third quarter of 2025.

claims.claim: Labor costs rose to 25.7% of revenue in Q3 2026, from 25.2% a year earlier.
claims.quote: Labor costs in the third quarter of 2026 were 25.7% of total revenue, an increase from 25.2% in the third quarter of 2025.

claims.claim: General and administrative expenses increased to 5.6% of revenue in Q3 2026, up from 4.9% in Q3 2025.
claims.quote: General and administrative expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $185.2 million… 5.6% of total revenue, compared to 4.9% in the third quarter of 2025.

claims.claim: Management cites “accelerating global expansion with entry into three new markets this quarter” as a growth catalyst.
claims.quote: …accelerating our global expansion with entry into three new markets this quarter.

claims.claim: Chipotle’s competitive environment includes fast‑casual, quick‑service and casual‑dining segments, with competition on taste, price, food quality, convenience, brand reputation and location.
claims.quote: The fast‑casual, quick‑service, and casual dining segments of the restaurant industry are highly competitive with respect to, among other things, taste, price, food quality and presentation, customer service, location, convenience, brand reputation, and cleanliness and ambience of each restaurant.

claims.claim: Chipotle’s competitors also claim higher‑quality, responsibly sourced ingredients, which could erode Chipotle’s differentiation.
claims.quote: We continue to believe our commitment to higher‑quality and responsibly sourced ingredients resonates with guests and gives us a competitive advantage; however, many of our competitors also make claims related to the quality of their ingredients…

claims.claim: Risk factors highlight the potential brand damage from food‑safety incidents, noting that Chipotle’s use of fresh, unprocessed produce and raw chicken may raise its exposure relative to some peers.
claims.quote: We may have higher risk for food safety incidents than some of our competitors because we use fresh, unprocessed produce, handle raw chicken in our restaurants, rely on employees cooking with traditional methods and don't use artificial preservatives or frozen ingredients…

claims.claim: The filing notes that compliance costs for federal, state and local regulations have risen but have not materially impacted capital expenditures or competitive position.
claims.quote: While costs associated with compliance with laws and regulations have increased as the number and scope of regulations have increased, the total costs incurred have not had, and are not expected to have, a material effect on our capital expenditures, results of operations or competitive position.

claims.claim: Supply‑chain risks include price volatility for key ingredients (beef, avocados, chicken) and potential shortages, which could force temporary menu item suspension.
claims.quote: The prices for some of our ingredients, such as beef, avocados and other produce fluctuate… If the cost of one or more ingredients significantly increases, we may choose to temporarily suspend serving menu items that use those ingredients…

claims.claim: Management’s forward‑looking statements identify wage inflation, labor market tightness, and union organizing as key people‑risk factors.
claims.quote: Forward‑looking statements … include … wage inflation and state or local regulations mandating higher minimum wages; the competitive labor market, which impacts our ability to attract and retain qualified employees; the impact of any union organizing efforts …

claims.claim: Cybersecurity risk is highlighted, with management noting heavy dependence on IT systems for POS, digital ordering, supply‑chain tracking and payroll.
claims.quote: We are heavily dependent on information technology systems, including for point‑of‑sale and payment processing in our restaurants, digital ordering and order delivery, tracing ingredients…

claims.claim: The company expects cash from operations combined with cash and investment balances to be sufficient to fund ongoing capital expenditures and working‑capital needs for the foreseeable future.
claims.quote: We believe that cash from operations, together with our cash and investment balances, will be sufficient to meet ongoing capital expenditures, working capital requirements and other cash needs for the foreseeable future.

claims.claim: Management plans to use excess cash to repurchase shares, with $1.6 billion remaining under current authorizations as of Q3 2026.
claims.quote: As of September 30, 2026, $1.6 billion remained available under share repurchase authorizations from our Board of Directors.

gaps: The 10‑K does not disclose quantitative forecasts for the number of Chipotlane locations that will be operational by the end of 2026 beyond the management‑forward‑looking statement in line 42.
Specific details on the expected impact of AI‑driven technology on labor productivity or cost savings are not quantified in the filing; only the intention to leverage AI is described (line 187).
The filing mentions sustainability targets (e.g., 50 % reduction in Scope 1‑3 emissions by 2030) but provides no interim metric or timeline for 2026 progress (see line 349).
research.insight: Insight: Chipotle plans to open 350–370 new restaurants in 2026, with roughly 80 % featuring a Chipotlane, and add 10–15 partner‑operated sites internationally — EX-99.1 line 42: "•350 to 370 new restaurant openings, which includes 10 to 15 international partner‑operated restaurants. Around 80% of new company‑owned restaurants will have a Chipotlane"

observations: The company’s annual filing reports a modest increase in top‑line sales and operating earnings relative to the prior year, while the quarterly release shows a slowdown in operating margin and a dip in per‑share earnings for the most recent quarter.
Cash generated from operations remains solid and exceeds the amount spent on capital expenditures, indicating ample liquidity to fund ongoing expansion and share repurchases.
No interest‑bearing long‑term debt is disclosed in the annual facts, which limits the ability to calculate a leverage metric; the debt‑to‑equity field is therefore unavailable.

The quarterly release provides its own outlook, projecting low‑single‑digit growth in comparable restaurant sales for the full year and a sizeable pipeline of new restaurant openings, many of which will incorporate the drive‑through format.

Both the 10‑K and the 10‑Q are treated as unverified filings; the data extracted from the SEC facts may contain classification or mapping ambiguities, especially for property‑and‑equipment additions and debt tags.
gaps: The filing does not include a clear reconciliation of the non‑GAAP operating margin measure to the GAAP figure, limiting comparability.
The definition of “comparable restaurant sales” is supplied in the release, but the underlying calculation methodology is not disclosed, preventing verification of the reported growth rate.
There is no disclosed amount for current‑maturity long‑term debt, and the mapping for the debt tag is reported as not comparable, leaving the debt‑to‑equity ratio indeterminate.

advisor.thesis: Chipotle’s growth strategy hinges on expanding its footprint with a drive‑through‑style format and deepening digital engagement. The company is adding a substantial pipeline of new sites, many of which will feature the Chipotlane concept that improves guest convenience and margin potential. Digital ordering already represents a sizable share of revenue and is trending upward, supporting same‑store performance. Meanwhile, cash generation remains robust, the balance sheet is essentially debt‑free, and the firm continues to fund expansion and share repurchases from operations. However, comparable restaurant sales are projected to be flat, cost pressures from labor and food inputs are rising, and the anticipated benefits from AI and technology remain unquantified. Coupled with a valuation that reflects solid but unspectacular growth, the outlook suggests preserving exposure rather than adding to it.
risks: Food‑safety incidents could damage the brand and increase ingredient costs.
Wage inflation and tight labor markets may erode margins despite internal scheduling tools.
Intense competition across fast‑casual, quick‑service and casual‑dining segments could limit price‑setting power.
Supply‑chain volatility for key ingredients may force menu adjustments and squeeze profitability.
Cybersecurity breaches or technology failures could disrupt ordering platforms and damage guest trust.
Uncertainty around the realized impact of AI‑driven efficiencies and the speed of Chipotlane roll‑out.
